review_notes: I read the whole file and grepped the ringed-spaces library for uses of the pure-tensor evaluation lemmas. I also checked how many `@[simp]` attributes the library uses elsewhere (77 occurrences in 14 files); this file has none. I looked at downstream uses in PresheafChangeOfRingsSymmetry.lean (lines 301 and 405) and SheafChangeOfRings.lean. I could not run Lean, so I did not test whether the proposed simp attributes make the proofs close, or whether they interact with Mathlib simp lemmas about `ModuleCat.extendScalars` or `restrictScalars`. The orientations I propose all move from a `tensorRestriction`, `tensorSectionMap` or `homEquiv` application to the explicit `tensorUnitSection` form. They shrink the term and have no obvious loop. `M.map f m` in the result could trigger `PresheafOfModules` simp lemmas, so adding the attributes should be checked by building.

findings.excerpt:
theorem tensorRestriction_unit (theta : A ⟶ B) (M : Presheaves A)
    {U V : Cᵒᵖ} (f : U ⟶ V) (m : M.obj U) :
    tensorRestriction A B theta M f (tensorUnitSection A B theta M U m) =
      tensorUnitSection A B theta M V (M.map f m) := by
findings.problem: These two lemmas, `tensorRestriction_unit` and `tensorSectionMap_unit` (line 220), are the canonical evaluation rules on generators `1 ⊗ m`. Both are oriented to compute: the right-hand side has no `tensorRestriction` or `tensorSectionMap` left, so a loop is not a concern. Neither is tagged `@[simp]`, so every use is a hand-instantiated `rw`. See the chain of three `rw [tensorRestriction_unit …]` at lines 208-210, the four-step chain at 249-252, and `rw [tensorSectionMap_unit, tensorSectionMap_unit, tensorSectionMap_unit]` at 282. Downstream, PresheafChangeOfRingsSymmetry.lean (lines 301 and 405) again calls `rw [tensorRestriction_unit]` and `rw [tensorSectionMap_unit]`. The same applies to `tensorSectionMap_smul` and `tensorRestriction_smul`, which handle the general `b • (1 ⊗ m)` case.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `tensorRestriction_unit`, `tensorSectionMap_unit`, and the `b •` variants `tensorRestriction_smul` and `tensorSectionMap_smul` as `@[simp]`. The `_smul` variants may need `map_smul` handled first, so check them separately. Then replace the `rw` chains at 208-211, 249-254 and 282 with `simp` or `simp [M.map_comp_apply]`. `tensorSectionMap_unit` is proved by `rfl`, so also consider `@[simp, reducible]`-style statement forms only if needed. Keep `change` steps only for the initial unfolding of `tensorPresheaf.map`.
findings.benefit: The pure-tensor normal form `tensorUnitSection … (M.map f m)` is applied automatically, so proofs about `tensorPresheaf` no longer list each instantiation by hand. Downstream proofs can use `simp` as well, and chains like `f ≫ g` reduce without naming each step.

findings.excerpt:
theorem tensorSectionHomEquiv_apply (theta : A ⟶ B) (M : Presheaves A)
    (U : Cᵒᵖ) (N : ModuleCat.{u} ((ringPresheaf B).obj U))
    (t : tensorSection A B theta M U ⟶ N) (m : M.obj U) :
    tensorSectionHomEquiv A B theta M U N t m = t (tensorUnitSection A B theta M U m) := by
findings.problem: `tensorSectionHomEquiv_apply` and `tensorSectionHomEquiv_symm_unit` (line 85) are the only characterisations of the section-level Hom equivalence. Each rewrites an opaque `Equiv` application into a term of the form `t (unit m)` or `g m`, so each reduces the term. Neither is a simp lemma. Every use is a manually instantiated `rw` with 4-6 explicit arguments: lines 306-309, 328-330, 385-387, 406-407, and in SheafChangeOfRings.lean:127. The proof of `tensorSectionHomEquiv_symm_unit` itself also works by rewriting backwards with the apply lemma (`rw [← tensorSectionHomEquiv_apply …]`).
findings.proposed_change: Tag `tensorSectionHomEquiv_apply` and `tensorSectionHomEquiv_symm_unit` with `@[simp]`. Together with `tensorRestriction_unit` and `tensorSectionMap_unit` they would give a terminating set: first the equivalence is unfolded to `t (unit m)`, then the unit rules apply. Then shorten the proofs of `tensorPresheafHomDown`, `tensorPresheafHomUp`, `tensorPresheafHomDown_naturality_left` and `tensorPresheafHomDown_naturality_right` to `simp` plus the naturality fact.
findings.benefit: Callers get a defined normal form for homomorphisms out of the tensor section. The `rw` arguments, which currently repeat `A B theta M U (N.obj U) …`, disappear from the proofs of the adjunction naturality lemmas and from SheafChangeOfRings.

evidence.excerpt: rw [tensorSectionHomEquiv_apply A B theta M U (N'.obj U) (t.app U ≫ k.app U) m]

findings.problem: The `map_id` proof does `rw`, then a non-terminal `simp`, then `rfl`. `simp` is being used to simplify `M.map (𝟙 U) m`, but it leaves a goal that only `rfl` closes. This suggests the simp set does not reach a canonical form for `tensorUnitSection … (M.map (𝟙 U) m)`. No lemma states that this equals `tensorUnitSection … m`, and the proof depends on whatever residue `simp` leaves. If a Mathlib simp lemma about `PresheafOfModules.map_id` or `ModuleCat.id_apply` changes, or if `simp` closes the goal, this proof breaks. `tensorPresheaf` is exactly where an `_obj`/`_map` simp interface is missing.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp] tensorPresheaf_map_unit` or rely on a simp-tagged `tensorRestriction_unit`. Also add a simp lemma `tensorRestriction_id` stating that `tensorRestriction A B theta M (𝟙 U) = 𝟙 _`, or the equivalent version on pure tensors. The `map_id` proof then becomes `simp` with no trailing `rfl`. If the `rfl` is unavoidable, make it a terminal `simpa` or `simp only [...]` with explicit lemmas.
findings.benefit: The proof becomes robust and its normal form is stated. A reader no longer has to guess what `simp` produced before the closing `rfl`.

findings.excerpt: theorem tensorPresheafAdjunction_unit (theta : A ⟶ B) (M : Presheaves A)
findings.problem: The file defines `tensorPresheafHomDown`, `tensorPresheafHomUp`, `tensorPresheafHomEquiv`, `tensorPresheafFunctor`, `tensorPresheaf` and `tensorPresheafMap` with no `_app`, `_obj`, `_map`, `_apply` or `_symm_apply` simp lemmas. As a result, every proof that uses them has to unfold by `change`. See lines 164-168, 205-207, 245-248, 268, 279-281, 302-305, 321-325, 383-384, 435-437 and 449-455, plus the `change` before `tensorPresheafAdjunction_counit`. Several `change` statements restate whole terms such as `(tensorSectionHomEquiv A B theta M U _) (𝟙 (tensorSection A B theta M U)) m`, which is costly to read. The lemmas `tensorPresheafAdjunction_unit` and `_counit` are simp-shaped (they evaluate unit and counit on generators) but are not tagged.
findings.proposed_change: Add the missing component lemmas. For example, `tensorPresheafHomDown_app : (tensorPresheafHomDown A B theta M t).app U = tensorSectionHomEquiv … (t.app U)` and `tensorPresheafHomUp_app`, which are `rfl`, and `tensorPresheafFunctor_map : (tensorPresheafFunctor A B theta).map h = tensorPresheafMap A B theta h`. Also add a `tensorPresheafMap_app` lemma, and mark `tensorPresheafAdjunction_unit` and `tensorPresheafAdjunction_counit` as `@[simp]`. Doing so would let the `change` blocks in the proofs be replaced by `simp`.
findings.benefit: The proofs of the naturality lemmas and the adjunction no longer hard-code the unfolded form of every definition. Users of the adjunction can reduce `unit.app` and `counit.app` on elements with `simp`.
